subject: English
passage: In the 1970s, Conor Flanagan emerged as an unconventional figure in classical piano performance. Most classical pianists maintained rigid posture and performed in formal evening wear with minimal audience interaction. But Flanagan would lean dramatically over the keys and perform in casual clothing. He would also select pieces that were traditionally played at moderate volumes and perform them with striking dynamic contrasts, alternating between whisper-soft passages and thunderous crescendos. Flanagan also modified these pieces by incorporating extended pauses between movements, allowing the audience to fully absorb the emotional impact of each section.
prompt: According to the text, what is one way that Flanagan differed from other classical pianists?

choices.A: He maintained rigid posture throughout his performances.
choices.B: He avoided pieces that were traditionally played at moderate volumes.
choices.C: He disliked incorporating audience interaction into his performances.
choices.D: He modified traditional pieces by adding extended pauses between movements.

explanation: Choice D is the best answer because it accurately describes an aspect of Conor Flanagan that the text indicates is unusual among classical pianists. According to the text, Flanagan differed from other pianists by incorporating extended pauses between movements, which allowed the audience to fully absorb the emotional impact.
